post.summary: Ingest up to 1000 ECS log documents in one request
post.description: Each log is validated on its own: valid logs are stored and invalid ones are reported in `errors` with their position, so one bad log does not reject the rest. Logs whose `event.id` is already stored for the same `service.name` are counted in `duplicates` and not stored again. If no log is valid the response is 422.

422.description: Invalid body, or no valid log in the batch

post.summary: Import raw logs: plain text, JSON or CSV
post.description:
The body is the file content. The format comes from `format`, or else from the Content-Type (`text/plain`, `application/json` or `application/x-ndjson`, `text/csv`).

Records do not need to be ECS: they are parsed and mapped to ECS.

* **text**: one record per line. Recognizes NDJSON, syslog (RFC 5424 and 3164), Apache/nginx access logs, klog, Kubernetes CRI, logfmt, and `<timestamp> <LEVEL> <message>` (Python logging, logback, log4j: also the logger and thread). Indented and `Caused by:` lines are added to the previous record as `error.stack_trace`. The raw line is kept in `event.original`.
* **json**: an array, `{"logs": [...]}`, one object, or NDJSON. Known schemas are translated: OpenTelemetry (OTLP/JSON), GELF, Serilog CLEF, Google Cloud Logging, AWS CloudWatch, Docker json-file.
* **csv**: header row with any column names; `,` `;` tab or `|`.

Any other schema is normalized: nested objects are flattened, names in any style (`traceId`, `trace_id`) are mapped to ECS, epoch and common date formats are read, a plain value where ECS has an object (`"error": "..."`) is moved to its main field, invalid service names and ids are fixed or moved to labels. What could not be kept as is is marked with a tag (`_message_missing`, `_timestamp_unparsed`, `_truncated`, `_fields_dropped`, `_level_missing`) or a label (`original_service_name`, `original_timestamp`). `service.name` and `log.level` fill in records that lack them. Like the batch endpoint, valid records are stored and invalid ones are reported with their line. Up to 10000 records and 5 MB; the file must be UTF-8.

422.description: Unreadable file, too many records, or no valid record

post.summary: Send a set of logs to the LLM for analysis
post.description: Select logs by `log_ids` (max 500) or by `filters` (most recent first, up to `limit`). The logs are grouped into patterns, sent to the configured LLM and the result is persisted. On LLM failure the analysis is still persisted with status `failed` and its id is returned in the error body.

LogCreate.title: LogCreate
LogCreate.description:
An ECS log document.

Accepts nested objects (`{"log": {"level": "error"}}`), dotted keys
(`{"log.level": "error"}`) or a mix. Required: `message`, `log.level`, `service.name`.
Any other ECS or custom field is accepted and returned as sent.

Send `event.id` to make retries safe: a log whose `event.id` is already stored for the
same `service.name` is not stored again.
